title: Operative Record
description: The output contract for one case. Your system writes one file per case at out/<case_id>.json validating against this schema. Extra properties are allowed anywhere; required properties are not optional. A null value means the transcript does not support a value, and is a legitimate, scored answer.

case_id.description: Must match the case_id in the source transcript.

fields.description: The structured operative record. Every field is present. A field the transcript never supports has value null, an empty evidence list, and whatever confidence your system assigns to that judgement.

procedure_performed.description: The procedure as completed, not as booked. A case that started laparoscopically and finished open is an open cholecystectomy.

converted_to_open.description: True if the laparoscopic approach was abandoned for an open one. Contemplating conversion is not converting.

cholangiogram_performed.description: True only if an intraoperative cholangiogram was actually performed. Discussing one, declining one, or describing when one would be indicated are all not performing one.

critical_view_of_safety.description: achieved_and_stated when the surgeon explicitly states the critical view was obtained. not_achieved when they explicitly state it could not be. null when the transcript never addresses it, which is the case the quality committee cares about most.

estimated_blood_loss_ml.description: Millilitres, as an integer. If the figure is revised during the case, the operative record takes the surgeon's final statement.

drain_placed.description: True if a drain was left in situ, false if placement was explicitly declined, null if never addressed.

specimen_disposition.description: Where the specimen was sent, in the transcript's own terms.

complications.description: An empty array and null mean different things and are scored differently. [] means complications were addressed and there were none. null means the transcript never addressed them at all.

counts_correct.description: The final surgical count. A count that was initially incorrect and then reconciled is a correct count.

cpt.description: Codes must exist in data/reference/cpt_codes.csv. A code your model recalled but the table does not contain is invalid, not merely unlucky.

review_queue.description: What the surgeon should look at, most important first. A system that returns an empty queue on every case is asserting certainty it does not have.

field.description: The field in question, or a dotted path such as coding.cpt.

reason.description: Why a human needs to look. Be specific: 'two conflicting statements' beats 'low confidence'.

note_markdown.description: The draft narrative operative note, in the institution's template. It must be derivable from `fields`: anything asserted here and not present there is an unsupported claim.

run.description: What this note cost to produce. Not optional.

models.description: Every model used, including any used only for verification.

mock.description: True when produced by --mock. Set it honestly; we check it at the live test.

evidence.description: utt_id values from THIS case's transcript. Every id must resolve, and the utterances must actually support the value. Citing the whole transcript is not evidence.

confidence.description: Your system's calibrated belief that this value is correct. It should be lower on the fields it gets wrong; we check that relationship, not the absolute number.

rationale.description: Why this code and not the neighbouring one. A payer reads this.
